newsitem.title: UK: UK rate hike seen unlikely to hit consumer mood.
newsitem.headline: UK rate hike seen unlikely to hit consumer mood.

text.p: The hike in British interest rates on Wednesday, the first since February 1995, is not likely to make a big dent in consumer confidence, but could temper investors' enthusiasm for stores, retail analysts said.
"The sector had been expecting a rate rise in due course, it's just come sooner than expected," said Tony Shiret, retail analyst at Barclays de Zoete Wedd.
"It may restrain the upside in the stores because people are aware that there's a monetary tightening now and could be a fiscal tightening after the election," he said.
Britain's ruling Conservatives must call an election by May next year.
Analysts said consumer confidence was notoriously difficult to assess, but they did not see the quarter-point increase in rates to six percent having much impact on Christmas spending.
"In the real world its very unlikely to have much impact," said Nick Bubb, retail analyst at Mees Pierson.
He said the powerful uptrend in consumer spending currently underway could easily accelerate, giving retailers a bumper Christmas.
Analysts saw the fall in some key retailers' shares as a knee-jerk reaction to the rate increase rather than any marked shift in sentiment.

By 1615 GMT Marks and Spencer Plc was eight pence lower at 514 pence, Boots Co Plc 12-1/2 pence lower at 616 pence, and Argos Plc down 11 pence to 771-1/2 pence. --Jane Merriman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
